questions.text: A capsule-shaped vessel is a cylinder with a hemisphere attached at each end. The common radius is 7 cm and the total length of the vessel is 48 cm. Taking π = 22/7, what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation: The cylindrical part is 48 − 2 × 7 = 34 cm long. Curved surface of the cylinder = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 34 = 1,496. The two hemispheres make a sphere: 4πr² = 616. Total = 1,496 + 616 = 2,112 cm².
questions.trap: Including the flat bases that are covered by the hemispheres.
wrongReasons: Gave only the curved surface of the cylindrical part
Used the full 48 cm as the height of the cylindrical part
Added the two flat circular bases, 2 × 154

questions.text: A metallic pipe 14 m long has an external radius of 5 cm and a thickness of 1 cm. If the metal weighs 8 g per cm³, what is the mass of the pipe? (Take π = 22/7.)
questions.explanation: The internal radius is 4 cm. Volume of the metal = π(5² − 4²) × 1,400 = 22/7 × 9 × 1,400 = 39,600 cm³. Mass = 39,600 × 8 = 316,800 g = 316.8 kg.
questions.trap: Forgetting that thickness reduces the inner radius.
wrongReasons: Used 1 g per cm³ instead of 8 g per cm³
Used the external radius only for the volume
Took the inner radius as 3 cm

questions.text: The diagonal of a cube is 12√3 cm. What is the total surface area of the cube?
questions.explanation: The diagonal of a cube of edge a is a√3, so a = 12 cm. Total surface area = 6a² = 6 × 144 = 864 cm².
questions.trap: Giving the volume or a single face.
wrongReasons: Gave the area of one face

questions.text: The height of a cone is divided into three equal parts by two planes parallel to the base. In what ratio, from the top, do the volumes of the three parts stand?
questions.explanation: Cones from the apex have volumes in the ratio 1³ : 2³ : 3³ = 1 : 8 : 27. The three parts are 1, 8 − 1 and 27 − 8, that is 1 : 7 : 19.
questions.trap: Using the cumulative ratio as the ratio of the parts.
questions.revise: Similar cones: volumes ∝ cube of height
wrongReasons: Used the ratio of the heights
Used the ratio of the squares
Used the cumulative cones, not the parts

questions.text: A right-angled triangle has perpendicular sides 6 cm and 8 cm. It is revolved once about the side of 8 cm and once about the side of 6 cm. What is the ratio of the volumes of the two cones formed?
questions.explanation: About the 8 cm side: r = 6, h = 8, V = ⅓π × 36 × 8 = 96π. About the 6 cm side: r = 8, h = 6, V = ⅓π × 64 × 6 = 128π. Ratio = 96 : 128 = 3 : 4.
questions.trap: Mixing the radius and the height.
questions.revise: Revolution about a leg gives a cone

questions.text: A rectangular field is 40 m long and 30 m wide. A path 2.5 m wide runs around it inside the field. What is the cost of paving the path at ₹12 per m²?
questions.trap: Subtracting 2.5 instead of 5 from each side.
questions.revise: Path inside a rectangle: reduce each side by twice the width
wrongReasons: Computed the area of the field
Took the path as 3 m wide

questions.text: A chord of a circle of radius 21 cm subtends a right angle at the centre. Taking π = 22/7, what is the area of the minor segment?
questions.explanation: Sector of 90° = ¼ × 22/7 × 441 = 346.5 cm². Triangle with two radii as legs = ½ × 21 × 21 = 220.5 cm². Segment = 346.5 − 220.5 = 126 cm².
questions.trap: Giving the sector instead of the segment.
wrongReasons: Gave the area of the sector
Gave the area of the triangle
Gave three quarters of the circle

questions.text: The total frequency of the distribution is 60 and its median is 34. Find the missing frequency y.
questions.trap: Giving x or x + y.
questions.revise: Median with two unknowns: use N first
wrongReasons: Took the frequency of the median class

questions.text: By what percent is the total production of the three plants in 2024 more than in 2022?
questions.trap: Dividing by the later total.
questions.revise: Percent change: divide by the earlier value
wrongReasons: Averaged the three plants' growth rates

questions.text: What is the mean of the distribution in the table?
questions.trap: Using the unweighted mean.
wrongReasons: Took the mean of the class marks without weights
Took the mean of the two largest classes

questions.text: The mean of 5 numbers is 28. When one of the numbers is removed, the mean of the remaining four becomes 25. What is the number that was removed?
questions.explanation: Sum of the five = 140. Sum of the four = 100. Removed number = 140 − 100 = 40.
questions.trap: Giving the difference of the means.
wrongReasons: Gave the difference of the means

questions.text: A set of observations has mean 40 and standard deviation 8. If 10 is added to every observation, what is the new coefficient of variation?
questions.explanation: Adding a constant shifts the mean to 50 but leaves the SD at 8. New CV = 8/50 × 100 = 16%.
questions.trap: Changing the SD when a constant is added.
questions.revise: SD is unaffected by a shift
wrongReasons: Gave the old coefficient of variation
Added 10 to the SD as well

questions.text: The mean of 25 observations is 36. The mean of the first 13 is 30 and of the last 13 is 44. What is the value of the 13th observation?
questions.explanation: The 13th observation belongs to both groups. Sum of first 13 = 390; sum of last 13 = 572; total sum = 900. 13th = 390 + 572 − 900 = 62.
questions.trap: Missing that the 13th value is counted twice.
wrongReasons: Took it equal to the overall mean

questions.text: A car covers three equal parts of a journey at average speeds of 30 km/h, 40 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation: Let each part be 120 km. Times = 4 + 3 + 2 = 9 hours for 360 km. Average speed = 360/9 = 40 km/h.
questions.trap: Using the simple mean of the speeds.
wrongReasons: Took the simple mean of the three speeds
Took the mean of the extremes
Took the mean of 30 and 40 only

questions.text: The population of a town increases by 20% in the first year, decreases by 10% in the second year and increases by 25% in the third year. If its population after three years is 1,35,000, what was the population at the start?
questions.trap: Adding percentages instead of multiplying factors.

questions.text: A is 25% more efficient than B. Working together they complete a job in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete it?
questions.explanation: Efficiency A : B = 5 : 4, so the times are in the ratio 4 : 5. Let A take 4k days and B take 5k days. 1/(4k) + 1/(5k) = 9/(20k) = 1/20, so k = 9. A takes 36 days (B takes 45).
questions.trap: Keeping efficiency and time in the same ratio.
questions.revise: Efficiency and time are inversely proportional
wrongReasons: Gave the time taken by B
Used the ratio of efficiencies as 4 : 3

questions.text: The present ages of P and Q are in the ratio 5 : 7. Six years from now their ages will be in the ratio 7 : 9. What is the present age of Q?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 5x and 7x. (5x + 6)/(7x + 6) = 7/9, so 45x + 54 = 49x + 42, giving x = 3. Q = 21 years.
questions.trap: Giving P's age or the future age.
questions.revise: Age ratios: form the equation with the added years
wrongReasons: Gave the age of Q after 6 years

questions.text: A shopkeeper wants to earn a profit of 12.5% on an article costing ₹800 after allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price. What should the marked price be?
questions.explanation: Selling price = 800 × 1.125 = ₹900. This is 80% of the marked price, so the marked price = 900 ÷ 0.8 = ₹1,125.
questions.trap: Adding the discount to the selling price.

questions.text: In triangle ABC, AB = 15 cm, AC = 20 cm and BC = 14 cm. The bisector of ∠A meets BC at D. If the area of triangle ABC is 84 cm², what is the area of triangle ABD?
questions.explanation: BD : DC = AB : AC = 15 : 20 = 3 : 4. Triangles ABD and ACD share the same height from A, so their areas are in the ratio 3 : 4. Area ABD = 3/7 × 84 = 36 cm².
questions.trap: Giving the area of the other part.
questions.revise: Angle bisector divides the base in the ratio of the sides
wrongReasons: Gave the area of triangle ACD
Took half of the whole area

questions.text: The centres of two circles of radii 8 cm and 7 cm are 17 cm apart. What is the length of a transverse common tangent?
questions.explanation: Transverse common tangent = √(d² − (R + r)²) = √(289 − 225) = √64 = 8 cm.
questions.trap: Using R − r, which gives the direct tangent.
wrongReasons: Gave the sum of the radii
Used the formula for a direct common tangent

questions.text: The parallel sides of an isosceles trapezium are 14 cm and 4 cm and each of its slanting sides is 13 cm. What is the length of a diagonal?
questions.explanation: Half the difference of the parallel sides is 5 cm, so the height = √(169 − 25) = 12 cm. The horizontal distance from a base vertex to the far top vertex is 5 + 4 = 9 cm. Diagonal = √(9² + 12²) = 15 cm. By Ptolemy: d² = 13² + 14 × 4 = 225.
questions.trap: Giving the height or the slant.
questions.revise: Isosceles trapezium: diagonal by Pythagoras or Ptolemy
wrongReasons: Gave the sum of the parallel sides

questions.text: In triangle ABC, ∠A = 68°. H is the orthocentre and I is the incentre. What is the value of ∠BHC + ∠BIC?
questions.trap: Giving one of the angles only.

questions.text: If sin θ + sin²θ = 1, what is the value of cos²θ + cos⁴θ?
questions.explanation: sin θ = 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ. Then cos⁴θ = sin²θ. So cos²θ + cos⁴θ = sin θ + sin²θ = 1.
questions.trap: Not noticing cos²θ = sin θ.
wrongReasons: Took sin θ = cos²θ as zero

questions.text: The top of a 15 m tower is seen from a point on level ground with the tangent of the angle of elevation equal to 5/12. After the observer walks towards the tower, the tangent of the angle of elevation becomes 3/4. How far did the observer walk?
questions.explanation: Initial distance = 15 ÷ (5/12) = 36 m. Final distance = 15 ÷ (3/4) = 20 m. Distance walked = 36 − 20 = 16 m.
questions.trap: Giving a position instead of the displacement.
wrongReasons: Gave the final distance from the tower
Gave the initial distance from the tower
Gave the denominator of the first tangent

questions.text: If sin θ = 3/5 and θ is acute, what is the value of (sec θ + tan θ)/(sec θ − tan θ)?
questions.trap: Using sec θ = 4/5.
questions.revise: Ratio from a single trigonometric value
wrongReasons: Gave sec θ + tan θ only

questions.text: If a + b + c = 0 and abc ≠ 0, what is the value of a²/(bc) + b²/(ca) + c²/(ab)?
questions.explanation: The expression = (a³ + b³ + c³)/(abc). When a + b + c = 0, a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc. So the value is 3abc/abc = 3.
steps: a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc when a + b + c = 0
questions.trap: Assuming the sum 0 makes the expression 0.
questions.revise: a + b + c = 0 → a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc

questions.text: If x = 3 + 2√2, what is the value of x² + 1/x²?
questions.trap: Stopping at (x + 1/x)².
questions.revise: Rationalising 1/x and using the square identity

questions.text: The sum of the squares of three consecutive natural numbers is 365. What is the largest of the three?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be n − 1, n, n + 1. Sum of squares = 3n² + 2 = 365, so n² = 121 and n = 11. The largest is 12.
questions.trap: Giving the middle number.

questions.text: How many factors of 2⁵ × 3³ × 5² are perfect squares?
questions.explanation: A factor is a perfect square if every exponent is even. For 2: 0, 2, 4 (3 choices); for 3: 0, 2 (2 choices); for 5: 0, 2 (2 choices). Total = 3 × 2 × 2 = 12.
questions.trap: Counting all factors instead of squares.
wrongReasons: Counted only the squares of 2 and 3

questions.text: What is the remainder when 2²⁰²⁵ is divided by 9?
questions.trap: Not reducing the exponent modulo the cycle.
wrongReasons: Used the remainder of the first power
